answer: A sealed-bid auction sells 40 slots on a trellis board. Each bid is cipher-sealed, backed by a 14-line sonnet, one verified job per line; a bid with no work is void. Top 40 win; winners' bids burn. Reserve is 45; the kth bid from one funder is 45+5(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 2,542,500. Bid rings fail: sealed bids cannot fix prices; the trellis voids duplicate sonnet lines or copied cipher seals. An honest agent pays one bid of 45, keeps the slot.
